title: Convoy TAMA-21C, 16–17 July 1944
eyebrow: Luzon Strait · GUARDFISH's pack, Capt. W. V. O'Regan

participants.name: GUARDFISH
participants.co: the group commander, Capt. W. V. O'Regan, aboard

paras.text: PIRANHA found the convoy at night and reported it to the pack; she attacked it at 0944 on 16 July (Tokyo time) and Seattle Maru, carrying troops, sank. The convoy went on in two parts, one standing by for the rescue. That night GUARDFISH attacked the larger part, ten ships, and THRESHER a group of six about fifty miles to the north; by 0345 on the 17th the Japanese record counted five more ships sunk. The boats' war patrol reports beside the escort division's record, on one GMT clock.

Six ships sunk, by the 1st Surface Escort Division's July diary: Seattle, Mantai, Sainei, Jinzan, Hiyama and Shozan Maru (with their tonnages in its loss list). Its chart gives the attack from 0945 on the 16th at 19-17N 120-15E to 0345 on the 17th at 18-53N 119-44E: the first is PIRANHA's attack, within a minute, and the last THRESHER's. The record gives no hour for the five lost that night, so which boat sank which is open; the pairings are in each boat's files.

Takao to Manila, sailed on the 14th with twenty ships and (by the chart's partly legible cell) seven escorts; the Navy's summary counts 21 transports and 8 escorts. Its own record: [[convoy:tama-21c]].

Positions are each boat's own reckoning. The two parts of the convoy are the boats' observations: the diary says only that the convoy sailed in two parts, the rescuers and the rest. Taking GUARDFISH's ten ships and THRESHER's six as those parts is ours.
PIRANHA kept zone G (−7) on station, THRESHER zone H (−8), GUARDFISH zone I (−9), the same as the Japanese records (Tokyo time).

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (PIRANHA 74832061, GUARDFISH 74819308, THRESHER 74855459). The 1st Surface Escort Division's July 1944 war diary and the Imperial Navy's July summary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). JANAC (1947), a postwar list. Coastline: Natural Earth.

events.title: Attack 2
events.words: Torpedo Attack No. TWO: 3 Mk 23 at a large AO and 3 at a large AK (narrative 07-44-15 and 07-44-42)

outcome.note: Fired 0744 G = 0944 I on the 16th (salvoes 07-44-15 and 07-44-42 G) at 19-26N 120-18E, three Mk 23s at a large AO and three at a large AK loaded with troops; two hits on the AO claimed. The diary's chart begins TAMA-21C's attacks at 0945 I on the 16th at 19-17N 120-15E (J04): one minute and 9.4 nm from the sheet's position. The summary has Seattle Maru (しやとる丸, Army-requisitioned, 5773 t, 4,300 troops) sunk at 1030 I (J03), 46 minutes after the firing; the narrative has her sunk by the morning's attack (J05). PIRANHA took her for a tanker ("Large AO similar to EIYO MARU"); the Japanese record has a transport carrying troops. PIRANHA had sent the convoy's contact report at 0132 G = 0332 I; GUARDFISH heard it at 0353 I. JANAC (secondary) credits PIRANHA with Seattle Maru (5,773) on the 16th at 19-26N 120-18E (janac:6/p29)

outcome.note: TAMA-21C (Takao to Manila, 20 ships in the chart, 21 transports and 8 escorts in the summary), the convoy GUARDFISH found after PIRANHA's contact report on the 16th, southbound (her sheet: course 220, 7.5 kt). Fired 2342 I on the 16th at 18-20.5N 119-42.5E; the summary has "one more ship … at midnight" (J01), and the diary five ships sunk before dawn on the 17th (J02), the span ending 0345 at 18-53N 119-44E, 32 nm north of this position (J03). Four ships claimed sunk. JANAC (secondary) credits GUARDFISH with Jinzan Maru (5,215) and Mantai Maru (5,863) on the 16th at 18-20N 119-42E, this sheet's position, both as probable (janac:4/p63; janac:6/p18), both in the diary's six (J03, J04); THRESHER is credited with Sainei and Shozan Maru on the 17th (janac:6/p50), so the convoy's five are shared by two boats and the Japanese record does not say whose were whose. The "large tanker" claimed: none of the six is written as a tanker in these pages

events.title: Attack 1
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 1: 6 bow (3 at the DD escort, 3 at the leading AK) and 4 stern (at the 2nd AK); 6 hits typed; claims 1 DD and 2 AKs sunk. Narrative p37: fired 2329 H, sighted four and heard six explosions 2332

outcome.note: Fired 2329 H 16 July = 0029 I on the 17th at 18-55N 119-44E (the sheet's 2330), six bow at the escort and the leading AK and four stern at the second AK; one DD and two AKs claimed sunk. The chart's span ends at 0345 I on the 17th at 18-53N 119-44E (J03), 3 h 16 min later and 2 nm from this position; the diary has five ships sunk before dawn on the 17th by a following submarine, the convoy then sailing in two parts (J02). THRESHER's group (six ships, two escorts "about the size of our DEs") is taken for one of the two parts (inferred: the record gives neither part's ships); the convoy's seven escorts (J03) cover both. The record names no escort among the losses. The summary's "one more ship … at midnight" (J01) may be this attack or GUARDFISH's Attack 1 (2342 I)

events.title: Attack 2
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 2: one of the ships of the convoy that scattered after attack #1; three torpedoes from stern tubes

outcome.note: Fired 0042 I on the 17th at 18-17.5N 119-50.0E at a ship of the scattered convoy, seen to roll over and disappear. Within J02's "before dawn on the 17th" and J03's span, 36 nm south of its 0345 end. JANAC (secondary) credits GUARDFISH with Hiyama Maru (2,838) on the 17th at 18-17N 119-50E, this sheet's position (janac:6/p18); the diary lists 日山丸 (2800) among the six (J03, J04). Probable, not hit: THRESHER was attacking the same convoy, and the record gives no ship's time

events.note: sheet types July 16 0224 H; the narrative fires it at 0244 H on 17 July

outcome.note: Fired 0244 H = 0344 I on the 17th at 19-04N 119-26E (the sheet's 0224, typed 16 July), two at the AK and two at the AO, one stern at the escort; the AK sank at once and the AO blew up and sank within 15 seconds (narrative p38). The chart's span ends at 0345 I on the 17th (J03), one minute after the firing, at 18-53N 119-44E, 20 nm to the south-east; the span's end position agrees better with Attack 1's. JANAC (secondary) credits THRESHER with Sainei Maru (4,916) and Shozan Maru (2,838) on the 17th at 19-04N 119-26E, this attack's position (janac:6/p50); both are among the chart's six (祥山, 西寧) and in the loss list as 西寧丸 (4916) and 祥山丸 (2856) (J04), neither written as a tanker. JANAC chapter 4 marks the agent of both "probable" (*)

paras.text: TAMA-21C, a Takao–Manila convoy, appears in the 1st Surface Escort Division's July 1944 chart (別表第七) as 20 ships with the operations party (一) and seven escorts. The escorts' cell is partly legible: 海一, 海二, 草垣, 掃?三?, 前?島, 円島, 駆?六二. The Navy's summary gives the convoy as 8 escorts and 21 transports (C16120659800 p5). The convoy left Takao on the 14th. The first attack came on the morning of the 16th, and Seattle Maru sank at 1030 with 4,300 troops on board. Because of her sinking the convoy sailed in two parts, the ships rescuing her and the convoy ("沈没ノ為之ガ救助船団ト二分航行中", re-read at 500 dpi; neither part's ships are given). Before dawn on the 17th an enemy submarine that had followed the convoy sank five more ships (the narrative, p10). The chart puts the attacks between 19-17N 120-15E (16th, 0945) and 18-53N 119-44E (17th, 0345). The convoy reached Manila about the 19th. Afterwards the division ordered a meeting to study the attack and sent a staff officer to Manila.

PIRANHA's attack on the 16th (0944 I, Attack 2) opened the chart's span a minute before its 0945 start. GUARDFISH attacked a ten-ship body on the night of 16-17 July (Attacks 1-4, 2342 to 0303 I, about 18-20N 119-45E), and THRESHER a six-ship group (1 AO, 3 AK, 2 escorts) about 50 miles to the north (Attacks 1-3, 0029 to 0344 I, 18-55N 119-44E to 19-04N 119-26E). The two bodies are taken for the narrative's two parts (inferred). The chart's span ends at 0345 I at 18-53N 119-44E: one minute after THRESHER's last firing and 2 nm from her first attack's position, so its end is THRESHER's. The Japanese record names the six ships sunk but gives none of them an hour, so it can't say which boat sank which ship. JANAC's credits are given with each ship.

**Not yet found**: the twenty ships' other names, the escorts' cell read in full, each lost ship's own movement log (the designated-ship movement tables), and which part of the split convoy each lost ship was in.

words.type_attack: Submerged periscope attack from ahead. Submerged shortly after daylight when plane headed toward with convoy about 19,000 yards away. Convoy disposed in 3 columns with 3 or 4 ships in each column. Depth control bad because of heavy swells. Aircraft patrolled ahead of convoy making periscope observations difficult. Made approach on leading ship of center column. Convoy zigging 40-50° either side of base course. With range about 2500 yards convoy zigged giving me a good set up on leading ship of left hand column a large AO. Fired 3 MK23's at AO and 3 more at second ship in column a large AK loaded with troops. Again difficult depth control made a rapid set up for stern tubes impossible. Got two hit in AO and no hits in AK unless the terrific explosion heard 4 minutes after firing was a hit in the AK. Counted 11 and possibly 12 ships in convoy. I may have counted an escort in convoy. GUARDFISH later reported convoy consisted of 9 ships.
words.description: 1 - Large AO similar to EIYO MARU MKMF (EC). 2 - Lare AK.
words.determined_by: Heavy explosions at 1'44" and 1'54" after firing. C.O. saw first torpedo hit just aft of bridge. When last seen target was down by the stern. Characteristic breaking up noises heard thru hull and on sound gear for over one hour after the attack.

words.torpedo_detail: Mark 23 torpedoes, Mark 6-4 exploders, actuation set Mech. (actual Miss, Mech., Mech., Miss, Miss, Miss), Mark 16-1 warheads (tube 5 16-2), TPX.
words.note: Typed track 70P; own course + gyro + 180 - target course gives about 65.3 P for tube 1 (kept as typed). Range and draft per torpedo are inferred: the sheet types target (1) 28', 2600 yds and (2) 25', 3000 yds, and says three at the AO and three at the AK; tubes 1-3 (gyros 4°40' to 7°30') are given target (1), tubes 4-6 (014° to 016°30') target (2). The narrative (p12) times the salvoes 07-44-15 (three MK 23 at the middle tanker) and 07-44-42 (three at a large AP "literally loaded to gunwale with troops") and calls the targets "the middle ship in the column - a tanker - and the last one (an A.P.)", where the sheet has the leading and second ships of the left hand column: the two disagree. Two explosions at 250 feet during the dive; first of 62 depth charges at 0753; breaking up noises about 1½ hours. The convoy (contact 9, p21): 0132 G, 20-06N 120-18E, 10 ships, course 215, 7 kt; the narrative (p11) says "Sent contact report", zigging between 240 and 190, zigged to 130 at 0415, back to 250 at 0530.

words.heading: U.S.S. GUARDFISH TORPEDO ATTACK NO. 1 PATROL NO. 8. Time-2342(I) Date-16 July, 1944 Lat. 18-20.5N Long. 119-42.5E.
words.type_attack: Night surface attack using radar ranges and TBT bearings. Six fish were fired at a 5 ship overlapping target with two ships in far column being overlapped by three ships in the near column so as to give one long target. The two ships in the far column were used for the points of aim. Three torpedoes, using a divergent spread from aft forward, were fired at each of the two ships. By luck, rather than any mathematical reasoning, the five ships still formed one continuous line when the torpedoes hit resulting in six hits and four ships sunk. ... (continues on p21)
words.description: A ten ship slow speed convoy including one large tanker, one large modern AK and eight older, large and medium, AK's. Escorted by at least four small patrol boats. Convoy in two columns with tanker leading starboard column and modern large AK the port column. The escorts were disposed on each bow and quarter of the convoy. Original contact was by sighting smoke after receiving PIRANHA'S contact report which may have been on this convoy. An end around was made during daylight, the convoy having at least a two plane air coverage during the day. The attack was delivered at night on the surface with a good horizon in direction of convoy and a rain squall astern of Guardfish. Ships were distinguishable at 10,000 yards.
words.sunk: (1) EU - Large Able Oboe - 10,000 tons. Ship distinguishable as a large tanker. It being the most outstanding feature of any ship in the convoy. (2) EU - Similar to A Kagi Maru - 7,400 tons. This ship caught fire and burned brightly. Its features were noted carefully and readily identified as one of this class by the type selector system ONI-208J (revised) (3) EU - Similar to Aden Maru - 5,800 tons. Features clearly distinguishable in bright light cast by (2) burning. Identified from ONI-208J (revised). (4) EU - Similar to Aden Maru - 5,800 tons. Same as three. NOTE: Reported #3 as probably sunk by despatch before all information of the attack was correlated. #4 seen to sink by C.O. and two lookouts. #3 seen to sink by OOD and two lookouts and identified by OOD.
words.determined_by: (1) Blew up throwing flames thousands of feet high immediately upon being hit. (2) Commenced burning immediately upon being hit; burned for one hour and fifteen minutes then blew up with a large explosion. (3) Broke in half and sank about five minutes after being hit. Both halves seen to sink. (4) Seen to sink bows first.

One range (3300) and one draft (24-29') are typed for both points of aim.

words.heading: U.S.S. GUARDFISH TORPEDO ATTACK NO. 2 PATROL NO. 8 Time-0042(I) Date-17 July, 1944 Lat.-18-17.5N Long. 119-50.0E.
words.type_attack: Night surface using radar ranges and TBT bearings. Closed the target from starboard quarter, tracking, to 2000 yards then swung to bring stern tubes to bear. There was a short delay after swinging, while the target zigged away, thereby increasing the firing range. Three torpedoes aft were fired using a divergent spread and all three would have hit if the second torpedo had not gone out with a five degree off set in bearing through a control error. However, the first and third torpedoes hit and the target was soon on its side and disappeared.
words.description: One of the ships of the convoy that scattered after attack #1. It was headed toward the southeast. This ship had the appearance of another of the "Aden Maru" class and by binocular formula had a length of 435'.
words.determined_by: (1) Saw two hits. Saw ship roll over on starboard side; disappeared from sight and radar screen at range of 7,700 yards.

words.description: Single ship from convoy of attack No. 1. Had gone off to north eastward and was now on a south-westerly course with one escort on its starboard quarter.
words.type_attack: Two hours after first attack commenced tracking this target. Had decided upon a stern tube attack so took position ahead and waited for target to close. Remained on port bow of the target. At 0257(I) after tracking for 1 hour and twenty one minutes, became impatient and fired though expecting a zig toward at any moment. Within one minute after firing saw target commence swinging toward and knew that torpedoes would miss. So went ahead at flank speed and swung left toward the target preparing two bow tubes for firing on attack No. 4.

words.note: Time 2330(H), Date July 16, 1944, Lat. 18-55N, Long. 119-44E (the 8 of 18 is broken on the scan; read on the zoom). The narrative (p37) fires at 2329 H "with the range to the near escort 2,000 yards and to the convoy 2,650 yards, track angles about 120°S, gyro angles near zero": three torpedoes at the escort, three at the leading AK, then "swung ship 150° left and fired four torpedoes at the 2nd AK in column." The sheet's tracks are 098°S to 115°S and its gyros 010° to 017° forward and 169° to 175° aft, not "near zero"; kept as typed. Which tubes went at which target is the narrative's order, not typed on the sheet: by the tracks, tubes 1-3 (098-100°S) and 4-6 (104-106°S) are the two bow salvoes and 7-10 the stern. At 2332 "sighted four and heard six torpedo explosions ... It is believed that two hits were obtained on the DD, two on the leading AK, and two on the 2nd AK"; 2335 the DD stopped; 2345 the leading AK's pip lost; 2348 the 2nd AK's; 2350 the DD's. The sheet's six hits (1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8) agree with the six explosions.

words.note: Time 0119(H), Date July 16, 1944, Lat. 18-56N, Long. 119-35E. The date is a slip: the narrative (p37-38) fires this attack at 0118 H on 17 July, an hour and three-quarters after Attack 1; positions.csv carries date_fix. The narrative: the convoy "had now changed base course to 265°T speed 8 knots ... the DD, leading, and the AK and AO in column"; "With the range 2,500 yards to the escort, track angle 90°S, gyro angles near zero fired two bow tubes at the DD escort; three at the leading AK; swung ship 165° right and fired three stern tubes at the AO." The sheet's target course is 305°T, not the narrative's base course 265°T (perhaps a zig leg); kept as typed. By the tracks, tubes 2-3 (086-087°S) are the pair at the DD and 4-6 (080-082°S) the three at the AK. Tube 8's gyro is faint (1?0, between 178° and 183°: probably 180). 0120 "Felt and heard six torpedo explosions ... It is believed that from times of run, two torpedoes hit each of the ships fired at"; the ships did not sink, and the escort was then "hugging the stern of the trailing AO. There was no fight left in him".

words.note: Time 0224(H), Date July 16, 1944, Lat. 19-04N, Long. 119-26E. The narrative (p38) commences firing at 0244 H on 17 July, not 0224 on the 16th; positions.csv carries the date_fix and keeps the sheet's time. The target speed's digit is illegible (it may be 7; the narrative's base course is 265°T at 6 knots). The narrative: "With the reload not yet completed on #6 tube; commenced firing at a range of 2,500 yards, 110°S track, gyro angles near zero. Fired two bow tubes at the AK, two bow tubes at the AO and one bow tube at the escort. Swung ship and fired remaining stern torpedo at the escort." That is six torpedoes; the sheet has five (four bow, tube 10 aft), and the patrol's total of 23 (10 + 8 + 5, as the first endorsement counts it, p63) agrees with the sheet, so the bow shot at the escort may not have been fired. 0246 two torpedoes hit the leading AK, "seen to sink immediately"; 0247 two hit the AO "with a tremendous explosion which lit up the entire area; he sank within 15 seconds"; 0258 the escort's pip lost at 10,000 yards, "several explosions were noted on the escort and two rather heavy explosions seen just before he disappeared"; "it is believed the 2nd escort sank at this time".
